issue_context.title: Custom error properties via schemas
comments: My recommendation for any application is to implement their own error handler and to no rely on the default one. I think we should not really make it smarter. However this functionality looks great and something that I'd like to use in any error handler. How could we make those easier to implement? In other terms, how could we make writing error handlers route-aware?

> How could we make those easier to implement?

I would try to think why a custom error handler is needed and, in my opinion, the use cases are:

- return a well-known (json) format --> the user set a response.5xx schema
- log and tracing --> it could be done by an `onError` hook
- obfuscate the error message --> it should be doable by managing the fastify config
- I18N/translation

has someone other use cases?

>  In other terms, how could we make writing error handlers route-aware?

The error handler has the request and its context, so all the schemas we need should be accessible internally, but not by the user that implement a custom error handler

----

Right now what I think is stressful and can be improved:

- if you set a custom error handler you must beware to log the error (we should do as request and reply does - adopting a pino `serializer`)
- if you set additional properties on the `Error` thrown and in the json schema output: nothing happens (and this can be fixed)
- the execution flow of the error should be better documented since it is not easy to understand without trying it (there are a bunch of use cases that could be better explained in the lifecycle doc - I'm working on it)

review_comments: These are a good start. However, a brief description of the function's purpose is also useful.
Sorry I thought I would be redundant on the `@return`, but I should have fixed now 👍

In particular on this function, the code is difficult to follow if you do not have any context around why it is invoked and what the function is attempting to achieve. So a description in the docblock would be very helpful on this one.
It'd be really helpful if we could start adding jsdoc blocks to functions like this one and `getSchemaSerializer`.
